To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The quantum matrices of intersecting loops are not independent, and that (ii) the commutator of two loops on a surface is given by an expression which depends on the intersection points and the holonomies of the loops.

(1) the quantum area phases are given in terms of holonomies of constant curvature connections; (2) the area phases satisfy the quantum Goldman bracket; (3) the area phases are invariant under homotopies; (4) the quantum area of an oriented loop is the same as the classical area; and (5) the quantum area is not invariant under orientation reversals.
We have developed a quantum version of the Goldman bracket for loops on surfaces in the context of (quantum) gravity in (2+1)-dimensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantisation of (2+ 1)–dimensionally Euclidean gravity. In particular
the quantization of (2+ 1)–dimensionual gravity.
the study of the quantization of the Chern–Simons theory on surfaces with boundaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work is an excellent contribution to the literature on quantum geometry, and the author is to be congratulated for his efforts in bringing this work to completion.
the quantum theory of 2+1 gravity, as described by a Chern–Simons theory, is a noncommutative deformation of the theory of 3–manifold invariants.

quantum geometry, in the sense that the quantum area phases are non-trivial and the quantum geometry is non-commutative, is a direct and inevitable consequence of the quantum nature of the holonomies of constant connection, and that the resulting non-commutative geometry can be expressed in terms of the quantum Goldman bracket for intersecting loops, which in the limit q → 1 reduces to the usual classical Goldman bracket for loops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed a noncommutative algebra of loops on a surface, which is the algebraic analogue of the algebra of functions on the moduli space of Riemann surfaces.
we are using the holonomies of constant (or “pure”) connections to construct a quantum geometry on the moduli space of flat connections.
we have constructed a quantum version of the classical theory of loops on surfaces which is consistent with the quantum gravity constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the area phases are not just a quantum correction, but are a necessary ingredient to the construction of a quantum geometry.
the quantum geometry of (2+3)–dimensional quantum gravity can be understood in terms of the quantum geometry of quantum Chern–Simons theory.
the quantum Goldman bracket for loops on a surface can be expressed as an area integral over the surface.
